label: <DEL> delimiter step (reset gate opens at the start of copying)
explanation: Fires almost only on the <DEL> delimiter step: 99.9% of activation mass and 99.75% of active steps fall there. It never fires during the original phase. In the copy phase it fires only rarely and weakly, on the first copied token when that token is x or z (161 steps, 0.1% of mass). It fires on about 64% of delimiters, and how often depends on sequence length: about 100% for L=3, 90% for L=4, 67% for L=5, 41-54% for L=6-8, and 83% for L=9. Delimiters right after a digit, or in sequences that start with a digit, fire less often (about 55% vs 64%). No simple token or length condition I tried improved F1 over phase==1, so which delimiter steps stay below threshold is not explained. The strongest activations come at <DEL> in short L=3 letter sequences, e.g. a i a <DEL>.
